context.title: The Gospel Reaches Cornelius
context.summary: A Roman centurion named Cornelius sees an angel. In Joppa Peter has a vision of unclean animals and hears that God has cleansed them. Peter goes to Cornelius's house, preaches, and the Spirit falls on the Gentile listeners.
context.background: Cornelius was a 'God-fearer', a Gentile who worshipped Israel's God, gave alms and prayed, without becoming a full convert. Jewish food laws (Leviticus 11) kept Jews and Gentiles from sharing meals. Peter was staying in Joppa, the same port from which Jonah once fled from God's call to the Gentiles.

customs.note: Tanning hides meant constant contact with dead animals, an unclean trade. Peter lodging there already hints at shifting boundaries.
Flat roofs offered a quiet, private place. The sixth hour was about noon.

watchFor: The vision is repeated three times (v. 16).
The Spirit comes before baptism, and Peter takes it as God's verdict (vv. 44–48).

people.name: Cornelius
people.summary: A centurion whose history is narrated in Acts 10. He was a “devout man,” and like the centurion of Capernaum, believed in the God of Israel.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: A Christian at Joppa, a tanner by trade, with whom Peter on one occasion lodged (Acts 9:43).

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: John
people.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

places.name: Caesarea
places.summary: (Palestinae), a city on the shore of the Mediterranean, on the great road from Tyre to Egypt, about 70 miles northwest of Jerusalem, at the northern extremity of the plain of Sharon.

places.name: Joppa
places.summary: Beauty, a town in the portion of Dan (Josh. 19:46; A.V., “Japho”), on a sandy promontory between Caesarea and Gaza, and at a distance of 30 miles north-west from Jerusalem.

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Nazareth
places.summary: Separated, generally supposed to be the Greek form of the Hebrew netser, a “shoot” or “sprout.”

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

events.title: Peter meets Cornelius
events.summary: Passage: Acts 10:1–33. People: Holy Spirit, Simon, Cornelius. Place: Joppa, Caesarea.

events.title: Peter preaches to gentiles in Caesarea
events.summary: Passage: Acts 10:34–48. People: Holy Spirit, Simon. Place: Caesarea.
